issue.title: Bug: Empty vector `[]` upsert with `wait=false` can trigger server panic (zero-length assertion failure)

repository.name: qdrant
repository.description: Qdrant - High-performance, massive-scale Vector Database and Vector Search Engine for the next generation of AI. Also available in the cloud https://cloud.qdrant.io/

issue.body:
## Summary

When upserting a point with an empty vector `[]` (zero dimensions) **without** the `wait=true` parameter, the API returns HTTP 200 with `"status": "acknowledged"`. While the point is eventually discarded during async processing, the zero-length vector can reach internal code paths that assert on non-zero length, causing **server panics** in distributed/sharded deployments.

This is distinct from the general "async upsert skips validation" issue (#2557, closed as not_planned) because empty vectors pose a **server stability risk** beyond mere poor diagnostics.

## Current Behavior

```python
import requests, time

BASE = "http://localhost:6333"

# Setup: create 4-dim collection
requests.put(f"{BASE}/collections/test", json={"vectors": {"size": 4, "distance": "Cosine"}})
time.sleep(0.5)

# With wait=true: correctly rejects empty vector
r_wait = requests.put(f"{BASE}/collections/test/points?wait=true", json={
    "points": [{"id": 1, "vector": []}]
})
print(f"wait=true:  status={r_wait.status_code}")  # 400 ✅

# Without wait: silently accepts empty vector
r_nowait = requests.put(f"{BASE}/collections/test/points", json={
    "points": [{"id": 2, "vector": []}]
})
print(f"wait=false: status={r_nowait.status_code}")  # 200 ❌
```

## Why This Is Different From #2557

I'm aware that #2557 (async upsert dimension validation) was closed as "not planned". This issue is filed separately because empty vectors are **qualitatively different** from wrong-dimension vectors:

| Aspect | Wrong dimension (e.g., 3→4) | Empty vector `[]` |
|--------|---------------------------|-------------------|
| Could be a typo? | Yes, off-by-one | No, zero dims is never intentional |
| Legitimate use case? | Arguably yes (migration) | No |
| Data stored? | No (discarded) | No (discarded) |
| **Can cause server panic?** | **No** | **Yes** — see #7967 |

The key difference: empty vectors can trigger **server crashes** in certain code paths, while wrong-dimension vectors are merely silently discarded.

## Evidence of Panic Risk

[Issue #7967](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/issues/7967) reports a production panic:

```
ERROR qdrant::startup: Panic occurred in file /qdrant/lib/common/common/src/fixed_length_priority_queue.rs at line 40:
length must be greater than zero
```

This panic occurs in `SearchResultAggregator::new` when a zero-length situation reaches the search path. While #7967's exact trigger was in a distributed context, the root cause is the same: zero-length data reaching code that asserts non-zero length.

### Source Code: Explicit Zero-Dimension Rejection

From [`lib/segment/src/data_types/vectors.rs`](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/blob/master/lib/segment/src/data_types/vectors.rs):

```rust
pub fn try_from_flatten(vectors: Vec<T>, dim: usize) -> Result<Self, OperationError> {
    if dim == 0 {
        return Err(OperationError::validation_error(
            "MultiDenseVector cannot have zero dimension",
        ));
    }
    // ...
}
```

The code **explicitly** treats `dim == 0` as a validation error. The problem is this check is only reached in the sync (`wait=true`) path.

### Source Code: Debug-Only Validation

[PR #8677](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/8677) review noted that `validate_vector_parameters` is only called inside `debug_assert!`, meaning **release builds skip this validation entirely**, allowing malformed vectors to reach deeper code paths.

### Version Consistency

| Version | `vector=[], wait=false` | `vector=[], wait=true` |
|---------|------------------------|----------------------|
| v1.12.1 | 200 (accepted) | 400 (rejected) |
| v1.18.0 | 200 (accepted) | 400 (rejected) |

## Impact

- **Server stability**: Empty vectors reaching internal code paths can trigger panics (#7967), crashing the service
- **Silent data loss**: Users receive 200 OK but data is discarded
- **Inconsistent validation**: `wait=true` rejects, `wait=false` accepts

## Proposed Fix

Unlike the general dimension validation issue (#2557), fixing empty vector handling has a **minimal performance impact** because it's a simple `vector.is_empty()` check at the API boundary:

```rust
// In the upsert handler, before writing to WAL:
for point in &points {
    if point.vector.is_empty() {
        return Err(OperationError::validation_error(
            "Vector cannot be empty (zero dimensions)"
        ));
    }
}
```

This is an O(n) check over the number of points (not dimensions), and `is_empty()` is a length comparison against 0 — essentially free. It does not require reading collection metadata or comparing against the configured dimension, so it doesn't affect the async throughput argument.

## Environment

- Qdrant version: v1.12.1, v1.18.0
- API: REST
- Deployment: Docker

## Related

- [#7967](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/issues/7967) - Server panic: "length must be greater than zero" in search path (Open, bug label)
- [#2557](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/issues/2557) - Async upsert doesn't return error for wrong dimension (Closed, not_planned)
- [#9039](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/issues/9039) - Re-report of #2557 with comparative analysis (Open)
- [PR #8677](https://github.com/qdrant/qdrant/pull/8677) - `validate_vector_parameters` only in debug_assert

issue.title: fix: validate vector dimensions before WAL write for async upserts

repository.name: qdrant
repository.description: Qdrant - High-performance, massive-scale Vector Database and Vector Search Engine for the next generation of AI. Also available in the cloud https://cloud.qdrant.io/

issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #9039

When upserting points with `wait=false` (the default), vector dimension mismatches were silently discarded during background WAL processing. The API returned HTTP 200 with `"status": "acknowledged"` but the points were never actually stored — causing silent data loss with no error feedback to the user.

This PR adds an early dimension validation check in `do_upsert_points()` that runs **before** the operation is written to WAL. This ensures dimension errors are returned to the client regardless of the `wait` parameter.

## Changes

- **`src/common/update.rs`**: Added `validate_vector_dimensions()` and helper functions that check vector dimensions against the collection's configured vector size before the operation reaches the WAL. Handles all vector types (dense, multi-dense, named, sparse).
- **`lib/collection/src/collection/collection_ops.rs`**: Added public `vectors_config()` accessor method on `Collection` to expose the vectors configuration for early validation.
- **`tests/openapi/test_vector_dimension_validation.py`**: Added integration tests verifying that dimension mismatches are rejected with HTTP 400 for both `wait=true` and `wait=false` upserts (point list and batch formats).

## Design decisions

- **Validation placement**: The check happens after inference/conversion (so embedding dimensions are resolved) but before `update()` writes to WAL. This is the earliest point where we have both the resolved vectors and access to the collection config.
- **Sparse vectors skipped**: Sparse vectors don't have a fixed dimension constraint, so they're intentionally excluded from validation.
- **Performance impact**: Adds one `RwLock` read of the collection config per upsert request — the same lock already acquired by strict mode checks on the same code path.
- **Error format**: Matches the existing error message format (`"Vector dimension error: expected dim: X, got Y"`) for consistency.

## Test plan

- [ ] Existing tests pass (the fix doesn't change behavior for valid operations)
- [ ] New test `test_vector_dimension_validation.py` verifies:
  - `wait=true` + wrong dimension → HTTP 400 (was already working)
  - `wait=false` + wrong dimension → HTTP 400 (was previously HTTP 200)
  - `wait=false` + correct dimension → HTTP 200 (no regression)
  - Batch format + wrong dimension → HTTP 400

issue.title: gRPC ingestion accepts NaN / +Inf / extreme-magnitude vectors — NaN scores rank above finite (silent HNSW corruption)

repository.name: qdrant
repository.description: Qdrant - High-performance, massive-scale Vector Database and Vector Search Engine for the next generation of AI. Also available in the cloud https://cloud.qdrant.io/

issue.body:
# gRPC ingestion accepts NaN / +Inf / extreme-magnitude vectors — NaN scores rank above finite (silent HNSW corruption)

## Summary

The default Qdrant ingestion path (REST `PUT /collections/{c}/points` and gRPC `Upsert`) accepts vectors containing `NaN`, `+Inf`, `-Inf`, or extreme magnitudes (e.g. `1e30`) with no server-side validation beyond dimension. Once persisted:

- `cosine_preprocess` propagates the corruption rather than detecting it (`sqrt(NaN) = NaN`, `Inf/Inf = NaN`, `1e30/Inf = 0`).
- `ScoredPointOffset::cmp` orders results via `OrderedFloat`, which places `NaN` **strictly above** every finite score. Consequence: a single poison point lands at the **top** of every unfiltered top-k.
- No log entry is emitted server-side.

Tested on `qdrant/qdrant:v1.18.1` (HEAD commit `e01c207`), `qdrant-client 1.18.0`.

This generalises and amplifies previously-reported issues #2530 (NAN vector → empty search), #4654 (Score NaN for zeroed uint8 vectors), and #9039 (async upsert silently discards dim-mismatched vectors). The pattern that #8130 asks for documentation about — *"ingestion incomplete … silent drift after re-ingest"* — is exactly this class.

## Reproduction

Full repro (docker-compose + Python): https://gist.github.com/Adelagric/285960fb998a3aa1247db03ff3e2e76d

Terminal recording (asciinema, 60s, anonymous upload, expires in 7 days): https://asciinema.org/a/Bn62N6QR6htNAZTx

Minimal inline:

```python
import numpy as np
from qdrant_client import QdrantClient
from qdrant_client.http import models as rest

client = QdrantClient(host="localhost", port=6333, prefer_grpc=True)
client.delete_collection("poison_demo")
client.create_collection(
    collection_name="poison_demo",
    vectors_config=rest.VectorParams(size=8, distance=rest.Distance.COSINE),
)

# One clean point to lock the dim
client.upsert(
    collection_name="poison_demo",
    points=[rest.PointStruct(id=1, vector=np.random.randn(8).astype(np.float32).tolist(),
                             payload={"label": "clean"})],
    wait=True,
)

# Four poison vectors
poisons = {
    "NaN_all":  np.array([float("nan")] * 8, dtype=np.float32),
    "Inf_all":  np.array([float("inf")] * 8, dtype=np.float32),
    "Huge":     np.array([1e30] * 8, dtype=np.float32),
    "Mixed":    np.array([float("nan")] + [0.5] * 7, dtype=np.float32),
}
client.upsert(
    collection_name="poison_demo",
    points=[rest.PointStruct(id=10+i, vector=v.tolist(), payload={"label": f"POISON_{n}"})
            for i, (n, v) in enumerate(poisons.items())],
    wait=True,  # forces synchronous error surfacing
)

q = np.random.randn(8).astype(np.float32).tolist()
res = client.query_points(collection_name="poison_demo", query=q, limit=10).points
for p in res:
    print(f"  {p.payload['label']:18s} score={p.score}")
```

### Observed output (from the linked repro)

```
POISON_Mixed        score=NaN
POISON_Inf_all      score=NaN
POISON_NaN_all      score=NaN   ← NaN-scored poisons fill the top-3
clean_B_1           score=0.525723
clean_A_0           score=0.380385
...
POISON_Huge         score=0.000000   ← 1e30 → normalised to all-zero, orthogonal score
```

A read-back via `scroll(with_vectors=True)` confirms the stored vectors:

```
POISON_NaN_all     [nan, nan, nan]  [NaN]
POISON_Inf_all     [nan, nan, nan]  [NaN]   ← Inf got mapped to NaN by cosine_preprocess
POISON_Huge        [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]          ← 1e30 collapsed to zero vector
POISON_Mixed       [nan, nan, nan]  [NaN]
```

And a kNN query whose vector itself contains `NaN` returns `score=NaN` for **every** point in the collection, clean ones included.

`docker logs qdrant | grep -iE "nan|inf|invalid|reject|warn|error|integrity"` reports nothing related to the four poisons. The 24-line log is silent on the corruption.

## Expected behaviour

At least one of:

1. The ingestion path rejects vectors containing `NaN` / `Inf` with a precise error (status `400`/`InvalidArgument`).
2. An opt-in `data_integrity_check: true` (or similar) on the collection's vector config triggers a finiteness pass + an optional `magnitude_bound` value, applied in `check_vector_against_config` for both dense and sparse paths.

The current `check_vector_against_config` is dimension-only:
- `lib/segment/src/common/mod.rs:188-219` (dense)
- `lib/segment/src/common/mod.rs:226-228` (sparse — explicitly TODO: *"`Ok(()) // TODO(sparse) check vector by config`"*)

## Root cause (code paths)

1. **gRPC decode** delivers a bare `Vec<f32>` without inspection: `lib/api/src/conversions/vectors.rs:179`. proto3 `repeated float data` is already binary IEEE-754 packed — there is no separate `vector_bytes` field, so any bit pattern the client emits lands in the buffer.
2. **Validator-crate validation** (`validator` declarative attrs) covers length/range only; no finiteness check: `src/common/update.rs:329-331`.
3. **Segment-level dim check**: `lib/segment/src/common/mod.rs:188-219` (`check_vector_against_config`). Dense only checks `vector.len() == config.size`.
4. **`cosine_preprocess` propagates non-finite components** rather than rejecting:
   `lib/segment/src/spaces/simple.rs:228-235`. One NaN component → `length = NaN` → `sqrt(NaN) = NaN` → division → fully-NaN vector persisted. `+Inf` component → `length = Inf` → `sqrt(Inf) = Inf` → `x / Inf = 0` for finite, `Inf / Inf = NaN` → partially-NaN vector. `1e30` per component → squared sum overflows to `+Inf` → all components normalised to `0.0`.
5. **`ScoredPointOffset::cmp` places `NaN` strictly above finite**:
   `lib/common/common/src/types.rs:23` (`OrderedFloat(self.score).cmp(...)`). The poison sits at the top of every `BinaryHeap`-backed top-k, and the HNSW build itself orders candidate links via `total_cmp` (`lib/segment/src/index/hnsw_index/links_container.rs:129,182,423,435`), so the graph topology can be skewed at construction time, not only at query time.
6. **Sparse path validation is incomplete**: `validate_sparse_vector_impl` (`lib/sparse/src/common/sparse_vector.rs:297-318`) checks only index/value count parity and uniqueness. No `is_finite` on `values`. `is_sorted` is a `debug_assert!` — release builds happily score unsorted sparse pairs and return wrong results.
7. **Quantization is exposed too**: `find_min_max_from_iter` (`lib/quantization/src/quantile.rs:19-33`) silently ignores `NaN` (comparisons return false) but accepts `+Inf`, which makes the SQ Int8 calibration `alpha = (Inf - min) / 127.0 = Inf`, encoding *every other vector in the segment* to `0`. One Inf vector at calibration time poisons the entire segment's quantized precision.

There is no `is_nan` / `is_finite` call anywhere on the dense ingestion path: `grep -rn "is_nan\|is_finite\|is_infinite" src/ lib/segment/src/{vector_storage,spaces,segment,segment_constructor} lib/collection/src/operations lib/api/src` returns no hit on the ingest path itself (only in `geo_hash`, `key_encoding`, `rescore_formula`, and `turboquant/quantization.rs:323` — none of which gate ingestion).

## Multi-tenant note (theoretical, not reproduced at small N)

With Qdrant's payload-filter-on-global-HNSW design (a single main graph per segment, plus optional payload-keyed subgraphs — `lib/segment/src/index/hnsw_index/hnsw/build.rs:116-279`), the tenant filter is applied **after** the greedy descent (`lib/segment/src/index/hnsw_index/graph_layers.rs:203`). With sufficiently many points to cross `full_scan_threshold`, a NaN ingested by tenant A would pollute the candidate heaps during tenant B's traversal. The linked repro contains only 14 points, well below the default 10000 threshold, so Qdrant uses exact scan and the filter is clean — this aspect needs a >10k-point setup to demonstrate empirically; I am not claiming reproduction here.

## Severity / impact

- Affects every Qdrant deployment that exposes REST or gRPC ingestion to potentially-untrusted clients.
- Any client with `CREATE`/`Upsert` permission on a collection can persistently:
  - Inject `NaN`-scored points that occupy top-k results for arbitrary queries.
  - Inject extreme magnitudes that collapse cosine-normalised vectors to zero (silently orthogonal).
  - At SQ calibration time, force `alpha = Inf` with a single `+Inf` vector → poison the whole segment's quantized precision.
- No log, no metric, no audit signal.
- Particularly relevant for deployments scoping their cloud under SOC 2 Type II / HIPAA — the public posture covers transport, isolation, access, encryption, but does not (and currently cannot) attest to vector-payload integrity.

## Environment

- Qdrant `1.18.1` (commit `e01c207`, default `docker-compose`, single node).
- `qdrant-client` `1.18.0`.
- macOS arm64, colima.

Happy to follow up with a PR introducing the opt-in finiteness + magnitude-bound check in `check_vector_against_config` (mirroring the same pattern across dense / sparse / quantization calibration), with a regression test that pins the current NaN-on-top ordering behaviour as a public contract that needs an explicit choice.
